Houston is down to its thinnest backcourt of the season at Washington: Fred VanVleet is ruled out on the first night of a back-to-back and Marcus Smart is still suspended, so more of the offense runs through Sengun. Clint Capela is still out and Steven Adams is only probable in his return, and Sengun has played 37 minutes in each of his last two games.

Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams, and Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, so Gilgeous-Alexander carries nearly all of the creation. Defenses have keyed on him with the roster this thin, and he played 39 minutes in Friday's one-point loss to the Clippers.

Boston hosts a Dallas team on the second night of a back-to-back after Kyrie Irving played 37 minutes at Cleveland on Saturday. Tatum leads Boston in every category and played 38 minutes in his last game; Dallas has not posted its injury report yet.

Atlanta is without Kingston Flemings (lumbar strain), Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye at Milwaukee, and Johnson's on-ball share is already up this season. He played 40 minutes Friday and is projected for his normal starting load. His game has a 233.5-point total.

Dallas is on the second night of a back-to-back at Boston, and Kyrie Irving played 37 minutes Saturday, so watch whether Dallas eases Irving's load. Clayton played only 13 minutes Saturday with Irving on the floor that long; Dallas has not posted its injury report yet.

Kingston Flemings, who started Friday, is out with a lumbar strain, which opens starting minutes on the wing. Dort started three games earlier this month when Jalen Johnson was out, and he went back to about 20 minutes off the bench once the lineup was healthy. His game has a 233.5-point total.
